Definition: from G2087 and G1100; other- tongued, i.e. a foreigner:--man of other tongue.
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, heteróglōssos means man of other tongue. It occurs just once, in 1 Corinthians.
TheologicalSignificance: I read heteróglōssos plainly: man of other tongue, and I leave it there.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
